A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide an analytical expression to characterize the best achievable accuracy of a range only localization system in a dense cluttered environment, and we show how to use this information to optimize the beacon deployment and the ranging estimation process.

the PEB can serve as a benchmark for the accuracy of a localization system, and that the relative importance and the impact of each beacon on the localization accuracy should be carefully evaluated before the system is implemented.

we derive a fundamental bound on the localization accuracy for UWB range only localization techniques in a dense cluttered environment, we investigate the impact of ranging estimation errors on the localization accuracy, and we investigate the impact and importance of NLOS beacons on the localization accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best positioning accuracy can be achieved when the information coming from all the beacons is used.
the PEB is a useful tool for designing and evaluating ranging based localization techniques in dense environments.
